newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe resigns as French premier, Jospin called in.
newsitem.headline: Juppe resigns as French premier, Jospin called in.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe formally resigned on Monday following his centre-right coalition's crushing parliamentary election defeat by the left-wing opposition, President Jacques Chirac's office said.
An official statement said Chirac would meet Socialist party leader Lionel Jospin at 11.30 a.m. (0930 GMT). He was expected to ask him to form a government.
Juppe, 51, in office since May 1995, had announced he would quit whatever the outcome of Sunday's decisive second round of voting following the right's debacle in the first ballot on May 25.

Jospin, 59, whose Socialist party and allies won 273 seats in the new 577-member National Assembly, was expected to form a broad-left coalition government, offering seats to the Communist party and the ecologist Greens.
The election ushered in France's third period of left-right "cohabitation" in 11 years between a president and a government of opposite political affiliations.
